Every Segment 110 field is separated by a Field Separator, including empty fields, which still send the Field Separator

MICR Data (Element 122) is required, alphanumeric, maximum 50 bytes, and required on all check transactions; when raw MICR data exceeds 50 bytes, only the first 50 bytes (left to right) are placed here and the remainder is expected in Extended MICR Data (Element 137), whose hosting data segment is not confirmed by the extracted Segment 110 table

Alternate MICR IND, documented in Section 12.9 as Segment 110 field 12 using element number 239, is optional, fixed 1 byte, and its only documented value is 'Y' (Alternate/RAW TOAD MICR format is being sent); this element number is separately defined in the Chapter 13 master element catalog as 'Enhanced Fleet Data' (999 bytes, used by Segment 145). Per SME decision (2026-09-26), both usages are modeled as distinct, segment-scoped entities (element 239 @ Segment 110 vs. element 239 @ Segment 145); this rule intentionally remains REVIEW_REQUIRED by design, not due to a gap

Two MICR encodings are documented in narrative text: Full MICR Line TAC format (example T999999999A999999999999999999C999999) and Full MICR Line RAW TOAD format (symbol substitution using T, O, A, D); Alternate MICR IND = 'Y' signals RAW TOAD/ALB1 format, but no machine-checkable grammar beyond the example and the 50-byte length limit is given

The MICR encoding convention for a manually keyed check is carried in Segment 111 (Variable Information Data Segment), not Segment 110: Variable Information Indicator = '024' (Manual Check MICR Type), Table Length fixed 2, with documented Table Data format codes 'T$' (T<aba>A<acct>C<checknum>), '18' (<aba><acct> concatenated), '09' (raw MICR, not touched), and '19' (numerals from bottom of check); Segment 110's MICR Data (122) and this Segment 111 sub-table are companions, confirmed independently of the AI-generated requirement set, which had attributed these codes to Segment 110 with LOW-MEDIUM confidence (44-47%)

Field order is Segment Type, Segment Length, SKU Data (only 3 fields; no field-ordering irregularity exists for this segment, unlike Segment 108)
All fields are separated by Field Separators; a Field Separator follows Field No. 3 (the last field); when a field is not populated, still send the Field Separator

The AI-generated relationship 'The Financial Transaction Request transaction includes SKU Data Segment (Data Segment No. 114)' (source_rule_id REL-ENT-SEG-114-FINANCIAL_TRANSACTION_REQUEST) is REJECTED as unsupported by Section 11.1.1's Financial Transaction Request Data Section 3 companion list, which enumerates only Segments 101, 102, 103, 104, and 111

Segment 115 is response-only: it appears only in the Financial Transaction Response and EMV Financial Transaction Response, never in any Request message
Segment Type is fixed value 115

Segment 115 maximum length is 1,009 alphanumeric characters (01-1,009/a-z/A-Z)
Field order is Segment Type, Segment Length, Print Data (only 3 fields; same shape as Segment 114)

Only two Field Separators exist in Segment 115: one between Field Nos. 1 and 2, and one between Field Nos. 2 and 3. There is NO trailing Field Separator after Field No. 3 (Print Data) — unlike every other segment documented so far (108, 114), which explicitly send a trailing separator
Segment 115 originates at the Host (every field's source is Host), unlike device-originated segments such as Segment 114

In the EMV Financial Transaction Response specifically, Segment 115 may co-occur with Segment 120 (Print Data 2 Segment) at Field 17/18/19, immediately followed by Segment 131 (EMV Response Data Segment) at Field 17/18/19/20

Whether Segment 115 can appear in the Loyalty Card Transaction Response (Section 11.2.2, which states it mirrors the generic Financial Transaction Response) is inferred but not explicitly restated for Segment 115
Segment 116 has a length range of 01-50 alphanumeric characters

Segment Length (Element 84) is present as Segment 116 field 2, following the universal Chapter 12 data-segment convention observed in every other defined segment (100 through 156); not independently confirmed by a Segment 116-specific table because Section 12.15 is a stub

The complete field-by-field layout of Segment 116 beyond Segment Type and Segment Length (i.e., what occupies the remainder of its 50-byte maximum) is not available in the current ATL105 extract; Sections 12.15 and 11.7.5 are both stub references to the external TransArmor specification-updates document

Segment Type (Element 85) is fixed value 118, Required, field 1

Information Byte (Element 44) is Required, field 4, 1 character, and indicates whether the request is a single-message or multimessage request; the complete value catalog is not shown in this workspace's source

Card Table Type (Element 174) is Required, field 10, 4 digits, identifying the specific table type this segment addresses, sourced from the Host and echoed back; valid values are 0001 (BIN Table), 0002 (RULES Table), 0003 (RESTRICTIONS Table), 0004 (SAF Table), 0005 (PROMPT Table), 0006 (PRODUCT Table)
When Prompt Code is 902 (Dynamic Card Table Data, response only), field 14 is Card Table Data (175, max 3,600 bytes, length determined by the Segment Length in field 2)

A Proprietary Data Load Request contains Data Section 1 (Elements 55, 63 with Number of Segments fixed value 1) and Data Section 3 (field 3, Segment 118, Required); it explicitly does not contain Data Section 2 / the Standard Message Data Segment (100)

Segment Length (Element 84) includes Segment Type's length and Field Separators, Device-sourced

Segment 130 originates at the device

Segment 130 has no trailing-optional-field omission allowance; all six fixed fields retain their Field Separators even when empty, and only the entire EMV Additional Information Section may be omitted

Segment 131 is response-only and conditional: it follows in the EMV Financial Transaction Response only when EMV data is required, alongside Segments 112 and 115/120
Segment Type is fixed value 131, sourced at the Host (contrast Segment 130's device-sourced Segment Type)

EMV Chip Data Length (Element 189) and EMV Chip Data (Element 190) are required, mirroring Segment 130's fields, but the field table lists their Source as 'Device' even though Segment 131 as a whole originates at BUYPASS

Settlement Type (Element 198) is required, 1 character, valid values D (Dual message), S (Single message), X (Non-traditional Signature Debit — availability must be confirmed with First Data Project/Relationship Manager)
Segment 135 is required only for transactions destined for the Moneris authorizer
Segment Type is fixed value 135, sourced at the Device

Segment Length Indicator is 3 digits, identifies the segment's length including Segment Type's length only (NOT explicitly including Field Separators, unlike most other segments' Segment Length description)

Segment Length Indicator is 3 digits, identifies the segment's length including Segment Type's length
A Field Separator follows the segment (i.e., a single trailing separator after the whole Segment 136, unlike Segment 135's per-field pattern)
Moneris Data (Element 213) is required, max 100 characters, in <tag><len><data> format; full layout documented in Appendix V (Moneris Data layouts)
Segment Type is fixed value 139, Segment Length is 3 digits, both sourced at the Device
Field Separator behavior is not explicitly summarized in Section 12.26 (no 'Note:' sentence, unlike Segments 135/141)
Segment 141 is used to close out each pay point to Moneris; it should be sent once for each pay point at day end
Segment 142 consists of a reiteration of the first 6 fields in the Segment 141 request, followed by a text response from Moneris
Segment Type and Segment Length are Host-sourced (contrast Segment 140's Device-sourced Segment Type/Length, and Segment 141's fully-Device-sourced request)

When a Financial Transaction request includes Segment 143, a Product Code Data Segment (Segment 102) MUST also be present, and each entry in Segment 102 should have a corresponding entry in Segment 143, in the same order
Only format validation is performed for this segment; no judgement is made of the values contained
Segment Type is fixed value 143, Segment Length identifies the segment's length including Segment Type's length and Field Separators, both Device-sourced, each followed by a Field Separator
Number of Products (Element 62) is required, 2 digits, and should match the number of products from the Product Code Data Segment

A dual-delimiter scheme is used: a Field Separator ('▲') follows the LAST tax amount for each product and signals moving to the next product (or end of segment for the last product); a Tax by Product Field Delimiter ('\') follows a tax amount when there is ANOTHER tax amount for the SAME product
A merchant may end a product's tax entry early (before 3 taxes) by using a Field Separator after the last reported tax entry instead of the '\' delimiter

Segment 145 carries fleet data for enhanced fleet offerings (Wex OTR, Comdata, Voyager EMV, Visa Fleet 2.0, MasterCard Enhanced Fleet EMV); it may hold multiple TLV-encoded sub-segments (sub-segment type, sub-segment length, sub-segment value)
Merchants should NOT send Segment 101 (Fleet Data Segment) and Segment 145 (Enhanced Fleet Request Segment) together in the same message

Only the Prompt Table sub-segment (Table ID 004) is valid for Voyager EMV, Visa Fleet 2.0, Comdata, and MasterCard Enhanced Fleet EMV transactions — other sub-segment tables (001, 002, 006, 007, 008) are restricted to different authorizer contexts not enumerated by this restriction
Segment Type is fixed value 145, Segment Length includes Segment Type's length; both Device-sourced

Enhanced Fleet Data (Element 239) is required, max 999 characters, containing one or more sub-segments in <tag><len><data> format, cataloged as: Table 001 (Request Flags, incl. Commercial/Retail Flag), Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Data, product-category-coded, '|'-delimited repeating), Table 004 (Prompt Data, authorizer-specific prompt tokens, '|'-delimited repeating), Table 006 (Money Code Payee Name), Table 007 (Money Code Check Number, required for all Money Code transactions), Table 008 (Cash Advance Limit)
Segment Type fixed 146, Segment Length includes Segment Type's length; both Device-sourced (despite this being a response segment, mirroring the sourcing pattern already flagged for Segments 131/136)
Table 002 (Non-Fuel Product Limits) is explicitly documented as NOT present in Comdata response messages
Segment 148 sends available product and fleet information from WEX to the terminal; appears in the Financial Transaction response for WEX transactions only
Segment Type fixed 148, Segment Length includes Segment Type's length; both Host-sourced

Segment 148 maximum length is documented as 23 characters in the opening statement but the valid-values range given is 001-999 — a numeric inconsistency; Available Product Information (Element 240) itself is 17 characters
Field Separators appear between fields 1-2, 2-3, and 3-4; the segment should end with a trailing Field Separator; data fields within field 4 (Price Data) are NOT separated by Field Separators
A Field Separator follows the segment (single trailing separator, per-field placement for fields 1-4 not explicitly documented)
Segment 151 can appear in ANY field slot of Data Section No. 3 (not a fixed position), originates at the device
Segment 151 maximum length is documented as 2,309 alphanumeric characters in the opening statement, but the valid-values range given is 01-3,334 — a numeric inconsistency
A Field Separator appears between each of the 3 fields
Segment Type fixed 151, sourced at Host (despite the segment overall 'originating at the device' per the opening statement) — a sourcing inconsistency

Segment Length is 4 digits (not 3), max 2300 characters; Market Basket Data (unnumbered element) consists of one DV dataset followed by up to 10 PI datasets, with full format defined in a separate 'Buypass Incomm Market Basket Data format' document
A Field Separator follows the segment (trailing separator, mirrors Segment 150's response pattern)
Segment Type fixed 152, Segment Length 4 digits, both Host-sourced
Market Basket Data consists of one DV dataset, up to 10 PI datasets, AND up to 10 PU datasets — one more dataset type than the request (Segment 151, which has no PU datasets)
Segment 153 contains Network Token Data for the transaction; may hold multiple TLV-encoded sub-segments (standard sub-segment type, length, value)
Segment Type fixed 153, Segment Length 3 digits (includes Segment Type's length), both Device-sourced
Segment 155 can only be sent when the transaction qualifies for, and uses, the First Data Auth Optimizer service
Segment 155 uses NO Field Separators — fixed-length/positional, same pattern as Segments 131/134
Segment Type fixed 155; the field table for fields 1-2 does not list a Source (unlike every other segment trained), an editorial omission
Segment 156 uses NO Field Separators — fixed-length/positional
EV Transaction Indicator (Table 01) is mandatory for an EV transaction and must be 'Y'; if the EV segment is sent without this indicator set to 'Y', BUYPASS will decline the transaction
Segment Type is fixed 156 and Segment Length is three numeric digits
EV Charging Data is required, max 200 characters, and consists of two-digit table IDs, three-digit lengths and matching table values
Segment 157 is used exclusively and allowed for Comdata cards only; any transaction containing this segment that is not for a Comdata card will be declined
Segment 157 is mutually exclusive with Segment 102 (Product Code Data); merchants should send one or the other but never both — if both are sent, the transaction will be declined
Fuel products must always be the first products in the segment; a maximum of ten products is allowed
Multi-fuel support: BUYPASS can accept transactions with multiple Fuel Type Codes in one transaction (e.g., Diesel + DEF + Reefer); the primary fuel must be the very first product code in the segment

A dual-delimiter scheme is used: Field Separator ('▲') follows Segment Type/Length and follows Adjusted Product Amount only when it is the LAST element in the segment; a Product Data Field Delimiter ('\') always follows Quantity and Unit Price, and follows Adjusted Product Amount when it is NOT the last element
Segment DL1 maximum length is 399 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host)

Segment DL1 uses NO Field Separators; instead it is self-delimited by a Data Type Indicator ('#', field 1) and an End-of-Data Indicator ('~', last field) — a distinct delimiting convention from the numbered segments (85/84 Segment Type/Length pair)
Segment DL1 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated, the next field immediately follows (no empty-position placeholder is kept)
Segment DL1 is Required in the Table Load Response, carried as Data Block No. 1 immediately after the Start-of-Data Block Indicator (Element 97, fixed ')'), and is sent only on a Table Load Response
Segment DL2 maximum length is 69 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host); Data Type Indicator fixed '!' (field 1), End-of-Data Indicator fixed '~' (last field)
Segment DL2 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated (Access Code, Pause Indicator) the next field immediately follows
Segment DL3 maximum length is 23 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host); Data Type Indicator fixed ':' (field 1), End-of-Data Indicator fixed '~' (last field)
Password (Element 65, 6 characters) is the only Device-sourced field in this segment, identifying the end-of-day function's password — every other field in Segment DL3 is Host-sourced
Segment DL3 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated, the next field immediately follows
Segment DL4 is used to download an application from a BUYPASS-supported device management system; vendors who support their own applications do NOT use this segment
Segment DL4 maximum length is 52 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host); Data Type Indicator fixed '@' (field 1), End-of-Data Indicator fixed '~' (last field)
Segment DL4 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated, the next field immediately follows

Segment DL4 is Required in the Software Load Response (Data Block No. 1, after the Start-of-Data Block Indicator ')'), is sent together with Segment DL5 (also Required), and is sent only on a Software Load Response; the load requires merchant load flag SOFT, otherwise only an error message block and a terminating block are returned
The device can attempt the automated full application load at most three times; if a load request to the Software Load Phone Number is unsuccessful, the device prints the 'decline' message
Segment DL5 is used to download an application from a BUYPASS-supported device management system via IP; vendors who support their own applications do NOT use this segment
Segment DL5 maximum length is 64 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host); Data Type Indicator fixed '$' (field 1), End-of-Data Indicator fixed '~' (last field)

Segment DL5 is structurally identical to Segment DL4 except field 4 is Software Load IP/URL Address (Element 114, 30 characters) instead of DL4's Software Load Phone Number (Element 91, 18 characters)
Segment DL5 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated, the next field immediately follows
Segment DL5 is Required in the Software Load Response as field 3, immediately after DL4 (field 2), and is sent only on a Software Load Response; the load requires merchant load flag SOFT

At the Software Load Request Date and Time the device accesses the Software Load IP/URL Address and requests the application load, with at most three attempts; an unsuccessful attempt prints the 'decline' message; after a successful load the device requests a Table Load
Segment DL6 maximum length is 9 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host); Data Type Indicator fixed '\' (field 1), End-of-Data Indicator fixed '~' (last field)
Segment DL6 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated, the next field immediately follows

Segment DL6 is Data Block No. 4 of the Table Load Response: it follows the End-of-Load Indicator '*' that closes Data Block No. 3 and is itself followed by an End-of-Load Indicator '*'; it is sent only on a Table Load Response

Segment DL7 is identified by the special character '^' (Data Type Indicator, Element 24) but, UNLIKE Segments DL1-DL6, does NOT use an End-of-Data Indicator; instead it uses a Segment Length Indicator (Element 84) to frame the segment, matching the pattern used by numbered segments (100-157) rather than the DL1-DL6 marker convention

Segment Length Indicator (Element 84) for Segment DL7 is EXCLUSIVE of the Data Type Indicator's length — a distinct counting convention from most numbered segments, which INCLUDE the Segment Type's length in their Segment Length
Download Data (Element 232, max 100 characters) is required, in <tag><len><data> format, with detailed layout defined in Appendix W (Download Data Layout)

The DL7 Segment Length (Element 84) is three digits — DL7 is not one of the seven segments allowed a four-digit Segment Length — and must equal the length of the segment content after the Data Type Indicator

Data Type Indicator is fixed value '%' (Element 24); Segment Length Indicator (Element 84, 3 digits) is EXCLUSIVE of the Data Type Indicator's length, same hybrid framing convention as Segment DL7 (no End-of-Data Indicator)
The DL8 Segment Length (Element 84) is three digits and must describe a whole number (1-24) of 26-byte Floor Limit Data groups after the Data Type Indicator
